NORTH CODORUS TOWNSHIP BOARD OF SUPERVISORS
July 7, 2026
Chairman Dennis Ilyes called the regularly scheduled meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.
Supervisors present: Jackson LeVault and Scott Meckley. Present on behalf of the Township:
Manager Melissa Altland, Zoning Officer Jeffrey Martz, and Solicitor Andrew Miller. Also
present: Recording Secretary and 11 citizens.
I. Announcements
If you are recording this meeting in any way, please announce that fact.
II. Agenda
No amendments to the posted agenda.
III. Minutes
Motion by Meckley, second by LeVault, to approve the minutes of the meeting of June 2,
2026. All members voted aye; motion carried.
IV. Treasurer’s Report
A. Motion by LeVault, second by Meckley, to approve the Treasurer’s Report for June
2026 as presented. All members voted aye; motion carried.
V. General Public Comment
Nothing at this time.
VI. Fire Company Report
Mrs. Altland gave the fire company report for June 2026. Wellspan EMS had 48 calls for
May 2026 and 49 calls for June 2026. Chicken barbecue, August 1, 10 a.m.; $12 per meal.
Motion by Meckley, second by LeVault, to approve the use of NCT fire police by West
Manheim Township for the Pleasant Hill Fireman’s Carnival on July 20-25. All members voted
aye; motion carried.
VII. Police Report
Chairman Ilyes gave the police report for June 2026.
VIII. Permits, Plans, and Modules
Deanna L. Neal, Final Subdivision Plan, Rohrbaugh Road
Chairman Ilyes will not vote on this plan, as the applicant is a relative. Mr. Martz
presented the information in the absence of the applicant’s engineer. This is a 73.1-acre property
that the applicant would like to subdivide 2 acres off (maximum allowable) to build residence.
Two waivers requested: Section 165-29.D.6, show existing features within 400’ and Section
165-30.G, wetlands study. Chairman Ilyes is familiar with the plan/proposal.
Motion by Meckley, second by LeVault, to approve the Final Subdivision plan for
Deanna L. Neal, Rohrbaugh Road. Two members voted aye; Ilyes abstained. Motion carried.
Motion by LeVault, second by Meckley, to approve the waivers requested to Sections
165-29.D.6 and 165-30.G. Two members voted aye; Ilyes abstained. Motion carried.

Page 2 of 3
Motion by Meckley, second by LeVault, to adopt Resolution 14-07-2026, planning
module for Deanna L. Neal’s subdivision. Two members voted aye; Ilyes abstained. Motion
carried.
IX. Administrative Reports
A. Supervisors’ Reports
No reports/comments.
B. Public Works – WWTP –
1. Motion by Meckley, second by LeVault, to ratify the replacement of the air
conditioning system at the WWTP, by Generation Plumbing at a cost of $12,185.00. All
members voted aye; motion carried.
2. Motion by LeVault, second by Meckley, to ratify the purchase of two bearing
flanges for the mower on the John Deere at a cost of $1,264.30. All members voted aye; motion
carried.
3. The duct work at the WWTP needs to be replaced. Not an emergency, but
soonish. Permission to Travis to gather quotes.
4. In August, the Sterling dump truck will be listed on Municibid.
5. The SBR transducer was replaced; a spare was ordered.
6. Line painting – Travis is having trouble getting line painting accomplished.
He’s looking into figuring out how the Township can do this instead of farming it out.
7. Future expenses: crew cab pickup; Travis is looking for a vehicle that all four
road crew members can fit in to go onsite somewhere. Motion by Meckley, second by LeVault,
to authorize Travis to investigate and possibly bid on the crew cab pickup truck NTE $20K. All
members voted aye; motion carried.
8. FYI, Met-Ed was here to discuss burying the lines from the Township to
Stoverstown Road. Met-Ed estimated over $13K to do this. Sounds like a lot.
B. Manager’s Report
1. Motion by Meckley, second by LeVault, to approve Resolution 13-07-2026, to
add the W.C. Myers Family farms, LP, to the Agricultural Security/Protection program; total
acres 79.66; only 9.67 acres in NCT. All members voted aye; motion carried.
2. Conrad Siegel pension – average 5.75% returns in 2025; currently funded at
102.7%.
3. PLGIT – Mrs. Altland met with Matt Conlin from PFM to discuss bank
accounts that the Township could use. The Board members would like to meet with Mr. Conlin
to go over some of this information. Mrs. Altland will set this up.
C. Engineer’s Report
Nothing discussed.
D. Solicitor’s Report
Zoning Ordinance Amendment – adopted in 2025 for AP and RAC, maximum lot
size 2 acres. Discussion was held. Attorney Miller will draw up a possible amendment at the
next board meeting.

Page 3 of 3
X. Old Business
Nothing at this time.
XI. New Business
Nothing at this time.
XII. Announcements
A. The Board of Supervisors will meet on August 4, at 7 p.m.
B. Northern York County Regional Police Commission will meet on July 21, 6 p.m., at
headquarters.
C. Planning Commission will not meet in July.
D. The Zoning Hearing Board will meet on July 16, 7 p.m. for the following cases:
26-01, Landing Opportunities, LLC, 2025 Stoverstown Road AND
26-02, Eichelberger’s U Pull It, 1395 Fire Hall Road and 1381 Sunnyside Road.
E. Comprehensive Plan Committee workshop will be held on July 20, 7 p.m.
From the audience, Kim Altland reported that several mailboxes in his area (Sunnyside
Road) have been hit by vehicles, perhaps farm vehicles or larger trucks. If the Township can do
anything to relieve this situation, it would be most appreciated. Please be advised that the
mailboxes are located in the ROW of the Township, and please check with the post office before
making any changes!
Motion by Meckley, second by Ilyes, to adjourn. All members voted aye; motion
carried. The meeting adjourned at 7:59 p.m.
Respectfully submitted,
Melissa Altland,
Township Secretary/Manager
Julie B. Maher,
Recording Secretary
